To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed, built, and tested a Snort intrusion filter that can be used in conjunction with Snort to prevent benign traffic in the network from being inspected by the Snort intrusion monitor.

(1) SIFT can process packets at 10 Gbps line rate and is able to filter 90% of benign traffic; (2) the hardware is reconfigurable and can be reprogrammed to support new rule sets; (3) SIFT can be extended to other packet types; and (4) a new method to measure the performance of an intrusion system is presented
we have implemented a snort intrusion preprocessor that can be used to prevent benign traffic, such as TCP SYN and TCP FIN packets, from being processed by a software-based Snort intrusion system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to design a high performance intrusion system that scales to support high-speed networks.
the design of a high-speed network intrusion detection and prevention system that is capable of inspecting a significant percentage of network traffic.
the design of high performance, high capacity intrusion detection systems that are capable of processing multiGigabit/sec traffic.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SIFT hardware is capable of inspecting 10 Gb/s of traffic, which is the current state-of-the-art in terms of throughput.
SIFT is a hardware implementation of a snort intrusion rule filter that can be used in front of an existing snort intrusion system to reduce the amount of traffic being processed by software.
SIFT is a snort intrusion system filter for TCP that operates at high speeds in FPGA hardware and provides the ability to selectively forward packets to a PC for complete intrusion processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that hardware intrusion detection and prevention is a feasible technology that can be used to protect high speed networks.
the SIFT system is a viable solution to scale intrusion detection and prevention systems for high-speed networks.
the SIFT system can process up to 1.2 Gbps of Internet traffic and can prevent 99.9% of benign traffic from being processed by Snort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hardware implementation of the SIFT system can be used to prevent the vast majority of benign traffic from being processed by software intrusion detection systems.
hardware intrusion detection is feasible for real networks.
hardware intrusion detection systems are viable and practical.
